newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end sharply up with soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end sharply up with soybeans.

text.p: Double-digit gains in CBOT soybean futures buoyed soy product futures to sharp gains at the close Monday, floor traders said.
The rally pushed all nearby soymeal months to fresh contract highs and boosted March soyoil to the highest level since January 16.
The markets' move through those key levels spurred fresh technically-inspired buying from funds, floor traders said.
"We spent the day trading inside of Project A's range and technically we got ahead of some key areas," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. brokerage.
All CBOT soy futures were supported by ideas that an impending strike at Brazil's Paranagua port would spread to other ports and slow export loadings, traders said.
Soyoil registrations shot up sharply Monday, which some saw as a sign that deliveries would increase. Soyoil registrations increased 1,997 contracts to 7,158.

CBOT soyoil futures ended up 0.17 to 0.30 cent per lb with March up 0.25 at 24.47 cents and May up 0.27 at 24.92 cents. Soymeal settled up $1.80 to $4.10, with March up $3.80 at $263.20 a ton and May up $3.90 at $258.60.
